Original Post: What Patches are there and do you recommend?. Hi! I've not played Arcanum for years and recently discovered that there are quite a few patches (and even mods?) out there.   
So I'm a bit confused - can you give me an overview of patches and maybe even recommend some?And do these patches work with different language versions, too?  


Thank you very much! :) User 1: At a bare minimum you'll want the 1.0.7.4 official patch. Options after that are all fan made. I recommend Drog's UAP (2.02) as it keeps the main game pretty much intact while fixing a ton of bugs and adding some nifty new content. There are a few mods that go after balancing issues but those heavily change gameplay so YMMV. User 2: What the other commenter said plus the wide-screen and graphic mods for towns. Unless those are included in the unofficial patch now.

Original Post: Caladon/Tarant Ending still bugged in latest Unofficial Patch?. Just completed my first playthrough in a couple of years - am I right in thinking the "***Caladon & Tarant Both at Peace***" ending is bugged, specifically the negotiations requirement?

From what I can tell, the ending checks your 'score' from the negotiations as to the stability of the two cities*. 

HOWEVER, the 'score' you get is how positive towards Tarant the outcome is, NOT the fairness of the arrangement. 

By following the 'balanced & fair' criteria outlined in the negotiating documents, you fail the Persuasion Master quest (which is understandable), but instead of the game marking 'both sides agree to fair terms' as the dossier makes clear, it instead flags 'negotiations went poorly'. 

So if you're trying to get the best ending for both, despite what the game is telling you, **you need to somewhat-but-not-completely** favour Tarant in the negotiations. 

Just wanted to flag this in case anyone is in the middle of a replay.



(*I'm including Don Throgg's election & returning the camera to Maxim as a given) User 1: I am not sure if I understand where is the bug (perhaps I only played patched version). As far as I remember: you receive quest for negotiations for Tarant, they want to screw Caladon as much as they can, but it's obviously better for the rest of the world if neither of these cities have major advantage on the other, so the best outcome and the end of the game is when Caladon joins the Kingdom but at pretty fair terms. Can't recall game ever telling me that for the sake of the Arcanum I need to screw Caladon (in fact, I think you can get persuasion mastery and still end up with the best ending - I believe I achieved it in my last playthrough) Am I missing something? Is there any mention in game that best for Tarant = best for the world? User 2: It's a feature, not a bug. It is possible to get mastery training AND the "good" ending, but it is a fine line to walk and you won't get the repudiation title. FWIW there are several competing quests in the game where you can only complete one or the other, not both. Or if you are able to complete them both you cannot do so with maximum results. &nbsp; On a side note, calling the endings "good" is relative ;) I think the industrial council is garbage for the half-ogre breeding program, but there is no way in game to punish them per se. My solution is to get the endings were Dernholm and Caladon win wars against Tarant, and where the sewers back up and throw the city into chaos. Bye-bye industrial council!

Original Post: Targets marked as obscured even though they're not?. Hey all, I've been playing Arcanum (my first time!), having a blast and shit, but I've encountered something that baffles me; I'm in the Tarant Sewers, killing Ghouls, but even when I have a clear, direct line of fire, the targeting icon for partially obscured target shows up and my accuracy is lower than usual (65% to hit instead of 85), but strangely, sometimes I feel like the penalty isn't there, hitting 4 or 5 shots in a row even though the penalty is displayed (though it could just be chance), even when I haven't changed my loadout.  This doesn't happen with any other enemies or areas.

Is this a known bug? Is there a mechanic I haven't noticed? Or are the sewers just like this? User 1: There are darkness penalties. Training with the Melee skill ignores these penalties, but I don't think that's the case with other ranged weapons. There are also tech vs. magick penalties, in firing a Firearm (or tech Bow, etc.) will come at a to-hit penalty against magickal enemies. I know certainly some types of ghouls class as magickal, others don't. That's about all I can think of off the top of my head. User 2: maybe this is the darkness penalty to accuracy??? User 3: There is also range penalties unless you have master firearms skill.

sentences: Vooriden. Vooriden. Location. The village is located at 868W 1191S, south-southwest of Tarant in the Morbihan Plains. It is marked on the player's map after accepting a quest from the ghost of Stringy Pete to free him from his curse. Temple of Halcyon. Rid Mr. Plough's Warehouses of Rats. Rid Mr. Plough's Warehouses of Rats. Rid Mr. Plough's Warehouses of Rats Start: Tarant, Simon Plough's Warehouse End: Tarant, Simon Plough's Warehouse Location: Tarant Rewards: 3,100 XP+Good alignment. Simon Plough in Tarant has recently bought a couple of warehouses, but it turns out that they are infested with rats. If you talk to him, he will ask you to clear the rats for him. He cannot offer you any rewards for doing so, but you can loot anything you find in there, plus you will gain quite a lot of experience for killing the monsters. Walkthrough. Talk to Simon Plough at the warehouse entrance and ask about his problem. Visit the smaller warehouse to the left first and kill the rats inside. You will also find a key in one of the barrels. Use the key to enter the bigger warehouse and kill everything inside. Return to Simon to finish the quest. Rewards. 3,100 XP +Good alignment

Exploits. Exploits. "Come with me Virgil, we must break the game."—Jesse (Troika Games). A bug, also known as a glitch is a mistake in computer software. In games, bugs are issues such as dissapearing items, repeating dialogue, missing dialogue, etc. Some use the term "glitch" only to describe visual errors such as missing textures or incorrect rendering. An exploit is a beneficial bug which can be "exploited" to give the player an unintended advantage. All bugs listed here are known to work on the latest official patch (1.0.7.4). If you are using an older version of Arcanum, please test the bugs you intend to post here to see if they work on the latest version as well. As always: SPOILER WARNING!. List of bugs, glitches and exploits. Bugs / Glitches. Arronax's Shell. Arronax's "indestructible" shell is actually just an untargetable object with a low HP, so it's possible to destroy it with AoE spells, although only visually. Arcanum ~ Arronax's Shell Glitch. Indoor Windows Glitch. Some separate map buildings (e.g. Bates' Mansion) have windows indoors for aesthetic purposes. Breaking these windows and then jumping out of them will allow the player to stand on the black tiles surrounding the map, but not be able to do anything remarkable such as walk all the way off screen on them (just 1 tile away from the wall). This is because there are no invisible blocking tiles set on the outer side of these windows. It may be possible to walk on the outer side of the walls and enter rooms which are ordinarily locked or otherwise inaccessible, although no examples of this have been found yet. Avoid Instant Kill in Falcon's Ache. By having Dweomer Shield or Reflection Shield cast on yourself when attacking the creatures or loggers in Falcon's Ache, you will not get instantly killed by the Quench Life-like spell. Disintegrate Glitch on Isle of Despair. If you are on theIsle of Despair and you challenge someone to fight in the pit and you kill them using the spell "Disintegrate" the game will glitch and not consider your kill counted and you will not be able to leave the pit. Yet Another Pit Glitch. Pit glitch. Permanent Stun Bug. If you play Fast Turn Based combat mode and get stunned by an enemy (such as Arbalah) just before they die, you may get stuck in a permanent stun. Your character will keep spinning in a state of dizzy confusion, and time will pass by very quickly. Even after waiting 5 minutes (in real life) the character was still stunned. It is worth noting that I was stunned multiple times, so this may have contributed to the glitch. I haven't tried replicating this, it seemed very odd and possibly random. To fix it, simply go to options and set combat mode to Real Time (press SPACE). Palette Issues. Casting Body of Air on a demon summoned through the Hellgate spell will cause it to permanently change its palette after Body of Air is cancelled from sustain. NPC Generator Issues. Stringy Pete. Stringy Pete. Stringy Pete Location: Stringy Petes Cove. "I don't talk much about him..I'll just say that Stringy Pete was the meanest, cold-blooded, murdering pirate who ever put to sail, and be done with it..there are stories and legends, and most of 'em are true.  He's been dead for more'n two hundred years, and people still whisper his name when they talk about him..". —Captain Edward Teach. The most cruel, ruthless and Ax-Crazy pirate of all times, feared all over Arcanum. He died more than two centuries ago, but rumors are that his spirit still sails the seas, punishing anyone who plays with his name..
